title: Ordinary big-small etale ringed comparison for algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes means [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its big etale site has every object and arrow of the fibred category, with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps, and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(x)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for $x$ over $T$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and morphisms of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. If $\mathcal C$ is such a category represented by an algebraic space $A$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], the inclusion of etale scheme charts gives a canonical morphism $\pi_A:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(A_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_A)$ whose module direct image is restriction $\pi_{A,*}H(T\to A)=H(T\to A)$. This module direct image is exact. For a functor $h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ over $S$-schemes between categories represented by algebraic spaces $A,B$, let $h_s:A_{\mathrm{et}}\to B_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the canonical ringed morphism with the module functors of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. There is a canonical ring-compatible commutation $\pi_Bh\cong h_s\pi_A$. Its direct-image comparison $t_h:\pi_{B,*}h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{s,*}\pi_{A,*}$ is the identification of compatible sections on etale scheme charts of $A\times_BV$, for every etale scheme $V\to B$, and preserves every such chart projection. It is natural in modules and test schemes. More generally, for any category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal E$ with the same big etale ringed site, any module $H$ on it, tests $z:A\to\mathcal E$, $w:B\to\mathcal E$, and an arrow $u:A\to B$ with a specified two-isomorphism $z\cong wu$, put $H_z(T\to A)=H(z|_T)$ on etale scheme charts. Restriction gives a natural comparison $c_{u,H}:u_s^*H_w\to H_z$, whose adjoint $H_w\to u_{s,*}H_z$ is restriction of the big-site adjunction unit $w^*H\to u_*u^*w^*H$, followed by $t_u$. These maps respect identities, composition, the specified two-isomorphisms, and chart projections. No algebraicity, quasi-coherence, flatness or finiteness assumption is imposed beyond representability of $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ by $A,B$.

source.place: Tag 073M (lemma-compare), Tag 073N (lemma-compare-morphism), equation-compare-big-small and Tag 076R (equation-comparison-algebraic-spaces-modules) with the following sentence. Exactness of the module restriction is the assertion used in the proof of Tag 075N, lemma-compare-morphism-cohomology.

proof.text: Choose the representing equivalence over $S$-schemes and write $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_A$: its objects are scheme maps $T\to A$, and its arrows are the commuting scheme maps. Precomposition by this equivalence and its quasi-inverse identify sheaves, their structure rings and all restrictions; the equivalence is over the same underlying schemes, so it preserves covers and regular functions. For the inclusion $i:A_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal S_{A,\mathrm{et}}$, covers and their pullbacks agree. Any big-site cover of an etale chart consists again of etale charts, by composition. Thus $i$ is continuous and cocontinuous. Fibre products of small charts are schemes and are computed by the same universal property in both sites. For parallel arrows $a,b:T\rightrightarrows V$ of small charts the equalizer is $T\times_{V\times_A V}V$, using $(a,b)$ and the diagonal. All these objects are schemes; the diagonal is an arrow between etale charts, hence etale by the scheme-test lemma, and its base change is etale. This proves existence and preservation of the equalizer. These verifications use only the stated algebraic-space and site definitions and the representable etale scheme-test permanence statements.

source.place: Tag 073M (lemma-compare), proof, construction of u and its connected-limit properties

proof.text: Let $R$ be restriction and $L=(i_p-)^\#$. The connected-limit lemma gives $L\dashv R$ and preservation of fibre products and equalizers. Check the missing terminal-sheaf condition as follows. Choose a surjective etale atlas $U\to A$ and put $P=U\times_AU$. For any big sheaf $G$, a map $1\to RG$ is determined by $s\in G(U)$ with equal restrictions in $G(P)$: on any etale chart, pull back the atlas and glue. The same pair describes a map $1\to G$ on the big site: for each arbitrary $T\to A$, glue the pullback of $s$ on the etale cover $T\times_AU\to T$; equality over $P$ is exactly the overlap condition, and uniqueness gives compatibility with every map of $T$'s. These are inverse constructions. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}(L1,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(1,RG)=\operatorname{Hom}(1,G)$ naturally; the canonical $L1\to1$ is an isomorphism. Products are fibre products over $1$, and finite limits are equalizers of maps between finite products, so $L$ preserves finite limits. It defines $\pi_A$ on sheaves of sets with direct image $R$. All sites and chart index categories are taken in the compatible universes fixed in the statement.

source.place: Tag 073M (lemma-compare), proof, final-sheaf argument with the atlas

proof.text: The equality $R\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal O_A$ is equality of regular functions and all restriction and ring operations on each chart. By step 2, $L$ preserves finite products, so the ring-object adjunction lemma makes $L\mathcal O_A$ a commutative ring object and shows that the adjunct $L\mathcal O_A\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ of the ring isomorphism $\mathcal O_A=R\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ is a morphism of ring objects; it equips $\pi_A$ with its ringed structure. By the definition of the induced module direct image its values and module actions are therefore exactly restriction. This restriction is exact: kernels are computed sectionwise, and a module epimorphism is locally surjective on underlying abelian sheaves. A section on an etale chart lifts on a big etale covering of that chart; every member of this cover is again etale over $A$, so it is already a covering in the small site. Thus restriction preserves epimorphisms as well as kernels. Here the generic module-sheaf lemma supplies exact faithful forgetting, sectionwise kernels and sheafified cokernels, and the general-site epimorphism criterion supplies the local lifts. No assertion about preservation of injective modules is used.

source.place: Tag 073M, omitted structural-ring check; Tag 075N (lemma-compare-morphism-cohomology), proof (2), exactness of restriction

proof.text: For $h:\mathcal S_A\to\mathcal S_B$ normalize by the representing equivalences as in step 1. Its functor over schemes is continuous and cocontinuous by the fibred-site lemma. The general cocontinuous adjunction computes $(h_*F)(V/B)$ as compatible families $s_{T,a}\in F(T/A)$ for all scheme objects $T\to A$ and arrows $h(T/A)\to V/B$, with compatibility under all such scheme maps. The two indexings are identical: such an arrow is precisely a map $a:T\to V$ with $h(T\to A)=(T\xrightarrow{a}V\to B)$. Equivalently these are all scheme maps to $X=A\times_BV$. The structure-ring pullback for $h$ is the identity on functions on each underlying scheme. The ringed module adjunction therefore gives this same compatible-family formula on modules, with $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ acting on a component through $a^\sharp$. This also proves that the big pullback on modules is precomposition. The unit sends a section to all its restrictions, as in the cited adjunction formula.

Compare the family of step 4 with the limit defining $(h_{s,*}RF)(V)$: the latter retains just the etale scheme charts $T\to X$. Indeed $X\to A$ is etale; a chart $T\to A$ with a map to $X$ is etale over $X$ by chartwise etale cancellation, and the converse follows by composition. Restricting the big family gives this small family. Conversely, from a compatible family on etale charts choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $Q\to X$. For an arbitrary scheme $T\to X$, the pullback $T'=T\times_XQ\to T$ is a surjective etale scheme map. Pull the prescribed section on $Q$ to $T'$. The two resulting sections on $T'\times_TT'$ agree because both pull back the equal sections on $Q\times_XQ$ prescribed by the original chart family. The big sheaf axiom gives a unique section on $T$. Pulling to the cover from a common atlas proves independence of $Q$; pulling the covers back along any $T_1\to T$ proves compatibility of these extensions. If $T$ was itself an etale chart, the glued section equals the prescribed one, by compatibility on $T'$. A big family is likewise recovered by this gluing, since it already restricts to the given section on $T'$. The two operations are inverse and preserve every chart projection. The fibre-product lemma and the scheme-test lemma ensure every covering object and overlap used here is a scheme; $X$ itself need not be one.

source.place: Tag 073N (lemma-compare-morphism), general case with U and R; equation-compare-big-small

proof.text: The inverse in step 5 commutes with addition and scalar multiplication: on $T'$ these operations are the operations on the restricted sections, and equality of the glued results follows by uniqueness in the sheaf axiom. On every component the scalar $r\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ acts by its image under $T\to V$, exactly the action defining the small chart limit. Hence this is an $\mathcal O_B$-linear isomorphism $t_h$. A module map commutes with every restriction used in gluing, so its two composites with $t_h$ have the same chart projections. For $V_1\to V$, restricting a compatible family is precomposing its chart maps with $V_1\to V$; both composites again have the identical chart projections. The limit universal property proves naturality. For sets the enlarged-etale ringed-site model computes $h_{s,*}G(V)$ as $\widetilde G(X)$, with its stated atlas equalizer. The chart-limit/enlarged-sections lemma identifies the chart-limit module direct image with the enlarged-model one by the unique isomorphism whose chart components are restriction from $\widetilde G(X)$, so the underlying sheaf of the module direct image is this set-level direct image, with the same chart projections. Thus the same gluing argument for sheaves of sets gives the direct-image isomorphism of geometric morphisms, with the underlying maps of $t_h$, whose inverse-image mate is the canonical commutation $\pi_Bh\cong h_s\pi_A$. For structure rings the formulas are ordinary pullback of functions on each chart, so this commutation respects the structural ring maps. Changing the representing equivalences gives the same chart maps and thus the same commutation up to its specified canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 073N and equation-compare-big-small, functoriality and structural-ring checks omitted in the source

proof.text: For the general tests $z,w$ of the statement, precomposition with the corresponding functors from the represented fibred categories makes $z^*H$ and $w^*H$ big module sheaves. This follows from fibred-site continuity and the cocontinuous adjunction, with identical structure rings, followed by the ringed module adjunction. Their restrictions are precisely $H_z,H_w$. Apply the unit of the big module adjunction for $u$ to $w^*H$, identify $u^*w^*H$ with $z^*H$ through the specified two-isomorphism, and restrict to $B$. Compose with $t_u$ to obtain $d:H_w\to u_{s,*}H_z$. Its small tensor-pullback adjoint defines $c_{u,H}$. More explicitly, on $V\to B$ a section $m\in H_w(V)$ has, under $d$, component $H(a)(m)\in H_z(T)$ at a chart $(T,a:T\to V)$ over $A$. Here the arrow in $\mathcal E$ uses the given two-isomorphism. The tensor-adjunction chart formula then gives $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,H(a)(m)$ on local representatives. This proves both the restriction description and the required unit-and-$t_u$ normalization.

Check coherence on the preceding formula. For an identity, $H(\mathrm{id})(m)=m$, so the tensor-unit identification $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$ gives the identity. For composable $u:A\to B$, $v:B\to C$, two successive local tensors are identified by the cited tensor-composition formula $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto a\,u^\sharp(b)\otimes m$. Their images under successive comparisons are $a\,u^\sharp(b)\,H(\alpha)H(\beta)(m)=a\,u^\sharp(b)\,H(\beta\alpha)(m)$, by functoriality of $H$ and its module action. This is the image for the composite comparison. The tensor formula is on local representatives generating the sheafified tensor products, so equality there implies equality of module maps by gluing; it does not assume global pure-tensor expressions. The prescribed two-isomorphisms identify the arrows $\alpha,\beta$ with the arrow for their composite, and applying the contravariant functor $H$ respects their composition. A map of $H$ commutes with $H(\alpha)$, and restriction to a further chart replaces $\alpha$ by its composite with that chart arrow. These give naturality and compatibility with two-isomorphisms and every chart projection. All uses of covers were etale base changes of atlases, and all other maps were arbitrary; no additional flatness, quasi-coherence or finiteness hypothesis occurred.
